This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Is there a constant $c>0$ such that every graph on $2^n$ vertices with minimum degree $>(1-c)2^n$ contains the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$?
#1035: [Er93,p.345]
graph theory
Erdős [Er93] says 'if the conjecture is false, two related problems could be asked':
Determine or estimate the smallest $m>2^n$ such that every graph on $m$ vertices with minimum degree $>(1-c)2^n$ contains a $Q_n$, and 
For which $u_n$ is it true that every graph on $2^n$ vertices with minimum degree $>2^n-u_n$ contains a $Q_n$.
See also [576] for the extremal number of edges that guarantee a $Q_n$.

 personally I find #181 more relevant (compared to #576). naive DRC says that $\approx 2^n(1-c)^{-n}$ vertices should at least suffice. and for fixed $c>0$, the arguments of Tikhomirov can show there is $c'\in (0,c)$ so that $2^n (1-c')^{-n}$ vertices suffice for large $n$.

 I'll note that the "blow-up case" should be clear here (at least if you want $m=(1+o(1))2^n$ vertices). 
let $H_0$ be any $m_0$ graph with minimum degree $>m_0/2$. by Dirac's theorem, $H_0$ should contain a Hamilton cycle, $C=v_1,\dots,v_{m_0}$.
now, consider consider the homomorphism $\phi$ which sends the $i$-th layer of the hypercube to $v_{i\pmod{m_0}}$. this is clearly a homomorphism, and the pre-image of any vertex has size $\sim 2^n/m_0$ (since the binomial coefficeints do not vary significantly).

 "the blow-up lemma" is a very deep result about doing spanning or nearly spanning embeddings of bounded degree $H$ into graphs $G$, based off of the regularity partition of $G$ (essentially if various parameters are right, we can embed $H$ as long as it has homomorphism into a certain auxiliary graph based on the partition). 
usually the bounds of various dependencies are fairly poor. but since we are embedding something bipartite (and just using pathwidth, rather than a more complicated), I could fathom it being possible for the bounds to work out (at least if we are willing to just aim for a nearly spanning embedding).
